quotes.text: A ticket is not a workflow. A ticket is a container for pain. It's a log entry that says something is wrong or someone wants something.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes ticketing versus workflow in a memorable, precise way.

quotes.text: Microsoft is the engagement plane. Capture intent, collaboration, communication, context. ServiceNow is the execution plane. Authoritative state, routing, approvals, evidence.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's split-brain architecture in two sentences.

quotes.text: And yes, AI can answer questions, that's useful, but answers aren't outcomes. AI without workflows creates noise. AI inside workflows creates outcomes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why assistants need governed workflows to deliver results.

quotes.text: So the pattern is simple, AI proposes, a workflow enforces, a human authorizes, the system records.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a reusable operating pattern for AI write operations.

quotes.text: And one non-negotiable boundary, the assistant can speak anywhere, but it can only write where you can audit it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp governance rule for AI assistants across platforms.

chapters.title: Beyond ticketing: the enterprise workflow problem
Tickets track pain, workflows control outcomes
Systems of record versus systems of action
Scenarios: onboarding, incident response, finance and major incidents
Connectors give answers, orchestration gets outcomes
Copilot and Now Assist: two brains, two jurisdictions
Failure modes: workflow entropy, shadow automation, permission drift
The workflow-first operating model in phases

takeaways: Tickets only describe problems; workflows are state machines that enforce sequence, ownership and evidence, which is the operating layer enterprises actually lack.
Microsoft 365 and Copilot should capture intent where people work, while ServiceNow and Now Assist own authoritative workflow state, approvals and audit trails.
Start with read-only integration, then move to governed write actions with least privilege and rollback, and only then to agentic execution, while watching for shadow automation and permission drift.
hook: Many organizations still treat ServiceNow as a ticketing tool and Teams chats as their process, so approvals, access and changes vanish into side channels. This episode is for enterprise architects and IT leaders who run Microsoft 365 alongside ServiceNow and want a clear split between engagement and execution, with Copilot, Now Assist and connectors governed so AI produces auditable outcomes instead of noise.
